title: POC scoping: Private networking & data residency - MedLink Health
next_steps: Redwood to share private networking checklist and region availability matrix
Customer to provide VPC CIDRs, current peering config, and egress policy documentation
Schedule benchmark run for week of 2027-01-04 (Redwood SE to run initial throughput/latency tests)
Follow-up security call to review SOC2 artifacts and KMS/HSM integration options
action_items: Sophie Patel: send private networking checklist, pilot pricing, and region map; due 2026-12-20
Ravi Kumar: share VPC CIDRs, peering routes, and egress constraints; due 2026-12-22
Daniel Wu: prepare benchmark plan (request patterns, seq lengths, models to test) and test harness; due 2026-12-28
Dr. Laura Benson: compile additional compliance Qs around data residency & key management; due 2026-12-24
header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Wu (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood), Emily Carter (MedLink VP Eng), Ravi Kumar (MedLink Cloud Ops), Dr. Laura Benson (MedLink CISO)
summary: POC scoping call to align on private networking and data residency requirements for a 4-week pilot. Main goals: confirm VPC peering vs PrivateLink approach, define regions (US-East, EU-West), capture egress and data residency constraints, and agree on benchmark success criteria (latency P95 < 250ms for 512-token seq, throughput target 80 req/s for initial dataset). Redwood to provide checklist, benchmark plan, and schedule security follow-up. Customer to provide networking details and compliance questions.
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off in a minute. quick roll call?
[00:08] Emily Carter: Emily here, hi Sophie.
[00:11] Ravi Kumar: Ravi on this end.
[00:13] Dr. Laura Benson: Laura here.
[00:15] Sophie Patel: great, thanks. Daniel and Priya from our side as well. the purpose today is to scope the POC around private networking and data residency for MedLink Health, specifically the pilot you mentioned in your RFP. want to confirm timelines, success criteria, and any blockers.
[00:34] Daniel Wu: yeah hi all, i'll own the benchmark plan. quick note — we typically run our pilot on a dedicated pool or a private deployment depending on egress needs.
[00:44] Ravi Kumar: to clarify, for us data must never leave the US for PHI processing. we need an option that keeps inference in us-east-1, and also need the ability to peer into our VPC or use PrivateLink.
[00:56] Priya Singh: understood. both VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink are supported, with slightly different network flows. PrivateLink tends to be easier from a security posture (no route table changes), peering gives lower cross-AZ latency in some cases.
[01:16] Dr. Laura Benson: on KMS — we require customer-managed keys. do you support HSM-backed keys and customer KMS in the private deployment?
[01:26] Sophie Patel: yes we support bring-your-own-KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated can be configured with CMEK. HSM integrations are possible with the private package — Daniel can give details.
[01:36] Daniel Wu: yeah we have a KMS integration pattern, we've done HSM-backed with a couple of healthcare customers. small caveat — during the initial pilot we use envelope encryption with customer KMS to keep secrets local.
[01:49] Emily Carter: timeline wise we want the pilot to run early Jan, hopefully start week of Jan 4 and wrap in 4 weeks to validate cost and latency. is that doable?
[02:00] Sophie Patel: that's tight but doable — we'll need your networking artifacts by Dec 22 to hit Jan 4 start.
[02:09] Ravi Kumar: what artifacts exactly?
[02:11] Sophie Patel: VPC CIDRs, route tables, whether you prefer PrivateLink or peering, list of subnets to allocate, and any egress proxy info — basically anything that influences routing and firewall rules.
[02:23] Ravi Kumar: we can get CIDRs and peering config. for egress we have a strict policy: only certain outbound IPs are allowed, traffic must go through our egress nat box which inspects TLS. can Redwood accommodate that?
[02:37] Daniel Wu: yes we can NAT through your egress or run inside a VPC with static egress IPs, there's a small setup step to ensure the serving fleet has the correct outbound IPs. note that static egress may add lead time for firewall changes.
[02:52] [crosstalk]
[02:55] Priya Singh: also note that if you choose PrivateLink we initiate a VPC endpoint in your account which removes the need to change route tables; traffic goes over AWS private backbone. that often aligns well with strict egress policies.
[03:10] Dr. Laura Benson: region question — we need processing for PHI to be in US only, but some non-PHI analytics are allowed in EU. can we split workloads by model endpoint region?
[03:21] Sophie Patel: yes routing rules can shard requests by policy — you can pin endpoints to us-east-1 for PHI and send anonymized analytics to eu-west-1. Daniel, can you confirm cross-region fallbacks?
[03:32] Daniel Wu: yep we support policy-based routing with automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. for the pilot we'll keep everything in us-east-1 to simplify. if you need cross-region later, we can test that in a follow-up.
[03:45] Emily Carter: success criteria — what should we measure? our internal asks: latency and correctness on our prompts, cost estimate, and stability under expected load which is around 80 requests per second peak for chat, average sequence 350 tokens.
[04:00] Daniel Wu: good baseline. for the POC we propose benchmarks: P95 latency for 512-token sequence under 250ms; sustained throughput of 80 RPS with 95% success; and qualitative evals on hallucination rates using your prompt sets. we will also measure cost per 1k tokens with a few model configs (fp16, q4, etc).
[04:22] Ravi Kumar: that P95 seems aggressive — do you think it's achievable with quantized models on a dedicated pool?
[04:30] Daniel Wu: it's dependent on model family. for smaller LLMs (7B-13B) optimized kernels and batching should meet that; for larger 70B+/context heavy loads we will likely see higher latencies and recommend dedicated capacity and different batching profiles.
[04:46] Emily Carter: our initial plan is to use a 13B optimized model and run our 350-token average. so sounds feasible. what's your data retention policy in a private setup?
[04:57] Sophie Patel: by default hosted API keeps logs for X days but for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention and disable retention entirely for PHI. we provide audit logs (who called what) and can pipe logs into your SIEM.
[05:12] Dr. Laura Benson: audit logs must be stored in our account or via our log sink. is that supported?
[05:17] Priya Singh: yes we support log forwarding to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver or an S3 bucket in your account in Private deployments.
[05:24] Ravi Kumar: about peering vs PrivateLink — performance delta?
[05:27] Daniel Wu: peering avoids the endpoint hops so latency can be slightly lower, but requires route table changes. PrivateLink gives stronger isolation and fewer infra changes on your side, sometimes slightly higher latency due to the endpoint. difference often in single-digit ms, depends on AZ placement.
[05:46] Emily Carter: any egress charges we should budget for?
[05:48] Sophie Patel: egress happens on our side for model downloads in private deployments during setup; typical bandwidth costs are passed through if large data transfers are required. for inference traffic inside a same-region VPC it's minimal. we'll include a rough egress estimate in the checklist.
[06:02] Ravi Kumar: security — SOC2 and penetration test reports?
[06:06] Sophie Patel: yes we'll share SOC2 attestation and a redacted pen test report in the security follow-up. also have an architecture whitepaper on our private offering.
[06:16] Dr. Laura Benson: about key rotation and KMS — do you support frequency-based rotation and audit trails for uses of the key?
[06:25] Daniel Wu: yes, with customer-managed KMS we defer to your key rotation policy and we log envelope key use in audit logs.
[06:33] Emily Carter: on benchmarks — can we run our actual prompts or must we use a synthetic harness?
[06:39] Daniel Wu: we prefer to run your real prompts in a sandbox during the pilot; we can anonymize PII if you prefer. that gives more realistic latency and quality numbers.
[06:49] Ravi Kumar: three questions: 1) will the pilot require dedicated GPUs or can a shared dedicated pool work? 2) how do you handle KV cache warmups for chat memory across sessions? 3) what's rollback plan if SLA isn't met?
[07:02] Priya Singh: 1) for consistent latencies we'd recommend a small dedicated pool for the pilot (2-4 GPUs depending on model), shared dedicated can work but more variance. 2) KV cache is sticky per session; we can pre-warm by seeding contexts for benchmark runs. 3) rollback — we have automatic fallback to hosted smaller model variants or to a cold path and will run a mitigation playbook; we'll include SLOs and escalation in the pilot docs.
[07:24] Emily Carter: what's the expected cost for a 4-week pilot with a 13B model on 2 GPUs? rough ballpark.
[07:31] Sophie Patel: rough estimate depends on instance type; i'll send a ballpark but expect pilot to be O(ten)s of thousands, not hundreds of thousands, for a narrow pilot. we'll include detailed pricing in follow-up.
[07:42] [pause]
[07:44] Daniel Wu: demo note — when we run benchmarks we'll measure token/sec, p95 latency, and tail latencies. also measure warm vs cold starts.
[07:54] Ravi Kumar: warm vs cold is important — our traffic pattern has diurnal spikes and many short-lived sessions.
[08:01] Daniel Wu: then we'll include burst capacity and autoscale profiles in the plan; also test prefix caching to reduce cost on repeated prompts.
[08:12] Emily Carter: any limitations with PrivateLink in multi-account setups? we have separate accounts for prod and staging.
[08:19] Priya Singh: PrivateLink supports cross-account endpoints; you'll create the endpoint in each account. peering also supports cross-account, but requires peering setup per VPC. we'll document both approaches.
[08:33] Ravi Kumar: compliance follow-up: can you sign BAAs for PHI?
[08:38] Sophie Patel: Redwood offers BAAs for Private deployments and Dedicated with the right contractual terms. we'll route that to Legal after the pilot scope is agreed.
[08:48] Dr. Laura Benson: in terms of data residency controls, we need throttles for any accidental cross-region routing. can we enforce pins per route?
[08:57] Daniel Wu: yes policy pins exist, you can restrict endpoints to region and model variant. we'll also add guardrails in the platform so accidental routing is blocked.
[09:08] Emily Carter: ok last practical: what does the benchmark test plan look like?
[09:12] Daniel Wu:plan: 1) ingest your sample prompt set (anonymized) 2) run steady-state load at 80 RPS with sequence dist (p25=120, p50=350, p95=512) 3) measure latency p50/p95/p99, token throughput, error rate 4) run cost model for fp16 vs q4 variants 5) produce report and recommendations — we aim to have results within 5 business days after environment setup.
[09:39] Emily Carter: sounds good. any blockers on our side to start?
[09:42] Sophie Patel: just the networking artifacts and compliance Qs. also please confirm the model family for initial run (13B opt).
[09:51] Ravi Kumar: we'll confirm 13B opt and send the network docs.
[09:55] Sophie Patel: perfect. i'll send the checklist and region matrix later today. Daniel will get the benchmark plan and Priya will send the security pointers.
[10:04] [longer pause as docs are shared in chat]
[10:10] Emily Carter: thanks everyone — recap and next steps?
[10:13] Sophie Patel: recap: Redwood to send networking checklist, region availability, pilot pricing, and benchmark plan. MedLink to provide VPC CIDRs, egress policy, and confirm model. schedule pilot start week of 2027-01-04. follow-up security call next week.
[10:30] Dr. Laura Benson: thanks, we'll review and come back with compliance Qs.
[10:34] Sophie Patel: great, talk soon.
[56:45] [call ends]
